title: Arithmetic & Order of Operations
summary: Real-number arithmetic — signed integers, fractions, and the order of operations (PEMDAS) — is the foundation for all of algebra. Master signs, common denominators, and the operation hierarchy so later manipulations stay error-free.

integer.plain: A whole number, positive, negative, or zero.

order of operations.plain: The agreed sequence for evaluating expressions.

fraction.plain: A ratio of two integers, part over whole.

common denominator.plain: A shared bottom needed to add fractions.
common denominator.in_class: Use the least common multiple of the denominators.

reciprocal.plain: The flip of a fraction; multiply to divide.

signed number.in_class: Same signs add; different signs subtract.

expression.plain: A combination of numbers, variables, and operations.
expression.in_class: Evaluated by the order of operations.

concept_sections.heading: Signed-number arithmetic
concept_sections.explanation: Adding numbers with the same sign adds magnitudes and keeps the sign; different signs subtract and take the larger's sign. Subtracting is adding the opposite; a product/quotient is negative only with an odd number of negatives.
math_steps: Same signs: add magnitudes, keep sign.
Different signs: subtract, keep the bigger's sign.
Products: count the negatives — odd ⇒ negative.

concept_sections.heading: Absolute value
concept_sections.explanation: The absolute value $|x|$ is the distance from $0$, so it's never negative. It appears in distance and error contexts and in solving $|x|=a$.
math_steps: Drop the sign to get the magnitude.

concept_sections.heading: Fractions
concept_sections.explanation: To add or subtract, get a common denominator; to multiply, multiply straight across; to divide, multiply by the reciprocal. Always reduce to lowest terms.
math_steps: Add/subtract: common denominator, then combine tops.
Multiply: across the top and bottom.
Divide: multiply by the reciprocal; simplify.

concept_sections.heading: Order of operations
concept_sections.explanation: Evaluate in the order PEMDAS: parentheses first, then exponents, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right.
math_steps: Then ×/÷, then +/−, each left to right.

concept_sections.heading: Evaluating expressions
concept_sections.explanation: Substitute values for variables, then apply the order of operations carefully — especially with negative substitutions and exponents on negatives.
math_steps: Replace variables with their values (use parentheses).

real_world_examples.title: Splitting a bill with tip
real_world_examples.scenario: Divide a total plus tip among friends.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Order of operations decides whether you add the tip before or after dividing — the grouping matters.

real_world_examples.title: Temperature swings
real_world_examples.scenario: Overnight the temperature drops below zero.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Signed-number subtraction finds the change: $|-5-8|=13$ degrees of swing.

real_world_examples.title: Scaling a recipe
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Multiplying each fractional amount by $\tfrac23$ uses fraction multiplication.
